text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
I'm working through the payoff structure of this public goods variant: tokens kept privately give 1 point to me but cost 0.9 points total to the other three members, while tokens placed in the group account appear to pay 0.3 points only to the contributor and don't affect anyone else's points—so it's less a shared pool and more an individual choice with external costs.

Comparing outcomes, everyone keeping everything yields 2 points per person from the own-vs-others calculation plus a flat 18, totaling 20, while everyone contributing fully yields 24—so cooperation is socially better even though keeping tokens is individually dominant (1 > 0.3). This is essentially a prisoner's dilemma: the rational one-shot move is to keep everything, but since this is a repeated game over 10 rounds, how others behave could shift what's optimal.

I'll go with keeping all tokens this round, since that's the self-interested dominant strategy, and explain my reasoning briefly.
